S&P 500

ES=F close · close 7,200.00

-2 stretched-down

ES=F closed 7200.00 on 24 November (from 7267.25, -0.93%) as the S&P 500 cash index fell 0.50% (-36.08) to 7,201.09, its eighth loss in nine sessions, giving back a tenth of Monday's 4.73% gain (CappNotes Closing Look, 24 November). The session was a rotation, not a liquidation: the Dow rose 0.85% (+423.39) to 50,018.70 - reported as its first close above 50,000, though one outlet says it had done so earlier in the year, a disagreement this ledger records rather than resolves since it does not score the Dow - while the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% (-356.03) to 23,733.54 and the Nasdaq-100 cash index 1.99% (-531.93) to 26,214.17. Breadth went the index's other way: 346 advancers to 154 decliners with nine of eleven sectors higher - Health Care +2.95%, Consumer Staples +1.66%, Real Estate +1.31%, Energy +0.97%, Financials +0.83% - against Industrials -0.53% and Technology -3.26%, and equal-weight RSP rose 0.54%, 104bp better than the cap-weighted index. The damage was concentrated in semiconductors: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 7.88%, SOXX 8.27% and SOXL 24.55%, with Nvidia -5.86% a day after +31.48% and still about 35% below its 6 October record close, Micron -11.01% on a downgrade to Neutral and high-bandwidth-memory demand worries, Analog Devices -17.37%, Semtech -16.97%, MaxLinear -16.74% and Hewlett Packard Enterprise -16.31%. Retail reported well - Abercrombie & Fitch +19.69%, Kohl's +19.48%, Dick's Sporting Goods +14.59% - and Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion, the largest pharma deal in three years, taking INSM +14.13% and Sanofi's US shares +10.97% (CNBC and news log, 24 November). The macro print was the surprise of the day: Conference Board consumer confidence rose 11.4 points to 103.3 against a forecast near 92.2 from an upwardly revised 91.9, its highest since January 2025, with Richmond Fed manufacturing at 3 from -2 and Case-Shiller +2.1% y/y (Kitco, 24 November). The VIX barely moved, -0.98% to 26.36. Treasuries firmed slightly - the 2-year unchanged at 4.63%, the 10-year about 1bp lower at 4.90%, the 30-year flat at 5.29% and 2s10s about 27bp from 29bp - and a $70 billion 5-year auction cleared at a 4.719% high yield with a 2.37x bid-to-cover against a 2.31x average and a 0.3bp tail, though indirect demand was reported as the weakest since March 2020. Credit tightened for the first time in this document's recent window: high-yield spreads 356bp, -11bp, and investment grade 94bp, -2bp. WTI reversed Monday's slide, +2.35% to $82.05, with natural gas +15.30%, while gold fell 2.64%, silver 5.65%, copper 2.53% and bitcoin 2.20%. RSI 39.32, with the close 5.9% below the 50-day (7648.08) and 2.4% below the 200-day (7380.24); 1H structure choppy, weekly structure uptrend.written Wed Nov 25, 9:45 AM ET · data through Tue Nov 24 close

why this stretch score
  • Two components fire for a score of -2 (stretched-down), down from -1 on 23 November. extension50 is -1: ES=F at 7200.00 is 5.9% under its 50-day (7648.08) for a z50 of -3.53 at a VIX of 26.36, short of the -4 that extension50 needs for -2. extension200 stays dormant at a z200 of -1.47 against a -6 threshold.
  • The second component is the crowd input at -1, the first non-zero volRegime or crowd value in this ledger's record. It is not a judgment call about how crowded the market feels: it records that two independent reports of the same Goldman Sachs prime-brokerage briefing, dated 23 November, themselves name percentile and multi-year extremes for US equity positioning - fundamental long/short net leverage of 42.3% at the 1st percentile of the past year on one account and the 5th percentile of one year and 3rd of three years on another, beta-adjusted net exposure at a 1st-percentile three-year reading described elsewhere as a five-year low, and the largest weekly single-stock shorting flow since June 2022. See nullInputs for the exact sourcing and the disagreement between the two accounts. At -1 rather than -2 the value is deliberately conservative for a figure that is one session old and reached through secondary reporting, and it changes no call in this document: all three equity cells are bullish, so the overlay reads them as opposing the stretch and leaves them untouched.
  • RSI 39.32, down from 41.40, is still well clear of the -1 oscillator threshold of 30, and the close sits 8.6% below the 252-session closing high (7874.00) and 12.7% above the low (6388.25), so the range component is dormant.

what's been moving this (3)
  • Market · High impact · Tue Nov 24, Pre-marketUS futures slip as Monday's record-setting Nvidia melt-up cools. Nvidia closed up 31.5% on Monday - its biggest one-day gain in 23 years - after reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, and the stock gives back about 5% premarket. Hewlett Packard Enterprise sinks on Q4 results while Dollar Tree jumps on a raised annual profit forecast; investors are still questioning whether AI infrastructure spending will earn its returns.
  • Market · High impact · Tue Nov 24, Pre-marketAsia staged a violent chip-led rally overnight on reports Nvidia had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, snapping eight straight sessions of losses for the regional benchmark. Korea, Taiwan and Japan led; Advantest, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and TSMC all surged. Europe then opened lower as the enthusiasm faded, with the FTSE 100, DAX, CAC 40 and Stoxx 600 all trading down (levels n/a).
  • Fed · High impact · Tue Nov 24, Pre-marketTreasury yields edge lower after an inflation warning from New York Fed President John Williams, who said policy 'will need to adjust' to get inflation back to 2% 'in a timely manner and on a sustained basis' and that 'there is still work to do,' adding the economy remains strong while inflation runs too high. Markets now fully price a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC. A $70B five-year auction and November consumer confidence are due today, with October core PCE on Wednesday the last major print before the meeting.
since the board (4) · news after Tue Nov 24 - not in these calls
  • Macro · High impact · Wed Nov 25, Pre-marketOctober PCE, the last major inflation print before the Dec 8-9 FOMC, came in hot. Headline PCE rose to 3.8% y/y, the highest annual reading since 2023, and core PCE accelerated to 3.3% y/y, above the 3.2% consensus and up from 3.1% in September. Consumer spending rose 0.3% m/m after an upwardly revised 0.6% in September. Traders now price a ~98% chance of a 25bp December rate HIKE from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, with another increase expected in January; Governor Waller has signaled he could back 50bp.
  • Policy · High impact · Wed Nov 25, Pre-marketThe Trump administration proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other major trading partners, following an eight-month USTR investigation into excess manufacturing capacity and industrial subsidies. The duties would stack on existing tariffs, pushing total rates above 40% in some categories, with China expected to face the higher end. Final rates are not set: the proposal goes through hearings and a public comment period and an official said it would likely take effect in January at the earliest. The existing US-China trade truce expires January 10.
  • Market · High impact · Wed Nov 25, Pre-marketMonday's Jensen Huang-return melt-up has fully reversed into a global chip rout. Asia closed sharply lower: the Kospi plunged 6.16% to its weakest close since Jan 13, triggering a sell-side sidecar on the Korea Exchange, while SoftBank sank about 14.8% to a 52-week low and dragged the Nikkei down 2.8%. Nvidia, which fell 5.9% on Tuesday, dropped another 5-6% premarket, with AMD, Intel, Micron and Dell all down more. Investors are again questioning the payoff on AI infrastructure spending and circular financing, with Anthropic trading below its $83 IPO price.
  • Macro · Medium impact · Wed Nov 25, Pre-marketThe BEA's second estimate put Q3 real GDP growth at a 4.3% annualized rate, a large upward revision from the 3.4% advance estimate and above the ~3.5% consensus, versus 2.2% in Q2. Quarterly core PCE was 2.5%, in line, and the GDP price index came in at 1.8%, below the 2.3% consensus. The release landed alongside October PCE at 8:30 AM ET, reinforcing the picture John Williams described on Tuesday: a strong economy with inflation still running too hot.

  • Market · High impact · Tue Nov 24, Pre-marketUS futures slip as Monday's record-setting Nvidia melt-up cools. Hewlett Packard Enterprise sinks on Q4 results while Dollar Tree jumps on a raised annual profit forecast; investors are still questioning whether AI infrastructure spending will earn its returns.
  • Market · High impact · Tue Nov 24, Pre-marketAsia staged a violent chip-led rally overnight on reports Nvidia had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, snapping eight straight sessions of losses for the regional benchmark. Korea, Taiwan and Japan led; Advantest, Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and TSMC all surged. Europe then opened lower as the enthusiasm faded, with the FTSE 100, DAX, CAC 40 and Stoxx 600 all trading down (levels n/a).
since the board (3) · news after Tue Nov 24 - not in these calls
  • Macro · High impact · Wed Nov 25, Pre-marketOctober PCE, the last major inflation print before the Dec 8-9 FOMC, came in hot. Headline PCE rose to 3.8% y/y, the highest annual reading since 2023, and core PCE accelerated to 3.3% y/y, above the 3.2% consensus and up from 3.1% in September. Consumer spending rose 0.3% m/m after an upwardly revised 0.6% in September. Traders now price a ~98% chance of a 25bp December rate HIKE from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, with another increase expected in January; Governor Waller has signaled he could back 50bp.
  • Policy · High impact · Wed Nov 25, Pre-marketThe Trump administration proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other major trading partners, following an eight-month USTR investigation into excess manufacturing capacity and industrial subsidies. The duties would stack on existing tariffs, pushing total rates above 40% in some categories, with China expected to face the higher end. Final rates are not set: the proposal goes through hearings and a public comment period and an official said it would likely take effect in January at the earliest. The existing US-China trade truce expires January 10.
  • Market · High impact · Wed Nov 25, Pre-marketMonday's Jensen Huang-return melt-up has fully reversed into a global chip rout. Asia closed sharply lower: the Kospi plunged 6.16% to its weakest close since Jan 13, triggering a sell-side sidecar on the Korea Exchange, while SoftBank sank about 14.8% to a 52-week low and dragged the Nikkei down 2.8%. Nvidia, which fell 5.9% on Tuesday, dropped another 5-6% premarket, with AMD, Intel, Micron and Dell all down more. Investors are again questioning the payoff on AI infrastructure spending and circular financing, with Anthropic trading below its $83 IPO price.
